why: Top-p 0.95 removes the tail tokens that start the cued base's 27 cap hits at T 1.0 while keeping its high-surprise exploration, so it gains about 11 over 410.

Min-p 0.1 is a sharper tail cut than top-p 0.95 at the high-entropy positions where the cued base goes off course, so it removes most of the 27 tail-started cap hits and lifts the 410 slightly more than top-p does.
Loops come from the tail, and the untruncated T 1.0 cell already has 0 rule-A loops, so cutting the tail with min-p cannot bring any back.
The 27 cap hits at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 are tail-token excursions, and min-p 0.1 removes the tail, leaving roughly the half that are just long problems.
Accuracy rises linearly with surprise (378 at T 0.6 to 410 at T 1.0, about +8 per 0.1 T), so T 1.5 adds about +40 over 410, while min-p 0.1 keeps the extra tail from causing excursions.
RL shares the base's tail-driven loop mechanism, so min-p 0.1 removes its T 1.0 tail excursions too and lifts it a few points above its 463 toward the 95 % ceiling.

High surprise does not make the plain base drift into garbled endings, so at T 1.0 the answers with nothing extractable are mostly the cap hits that remain once raising T has cut the T 0.6 cap hits (about 25), plus a few format misses.
At T 0.6 the plain base's 65-69 cap hits, set off by tail tokens it cannot explore its way out of at low temperature, each leave no final answer, and a few format misses come on top.
